messages.subject: Plotting function only
parts:
Hello,

I want to plot function f(x,a,b,c) where a,
b and c are coefficients I provide manually.
The shape of the function will look like
two superimposed normal distributions.
Is it generally possible to plot such a mathematical
function with ggplot (there is no dataset with
actual data, just the function of x and its coefficients).
If it is possible how? Maybe someone can just give
an example and print y=10+x^3 (in a specified range of x)

Thank you very much,

best regards,
Johannes

messages.subject: Re: Plotting function only
parts:
Sorry, I accidently only replied to you instead of reply-all'ing to
the list. Adding the list again.

Having never used stat_function, I looked it up:
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/stat_function.html

As it says: "To use these variables in an aesthetic mapping, you need
to surrond them with .., like aes(x = ..output..). This tells ggplot
that the variable isn't the original dataset, but has been created by
the statistic."

So I think you need something like ggplot(tmp, aes(x=..x.., y=..y..))
for the first part, and you need to write a wrapper for your function,
like

eq_tmp <- function(x) {
eq(x, sigma_stat, sigma_mob, p)
}

and use that in your stat_function.


On 5 December 2011 06:16, Johannes Radinger <JRad...@gmx.at> wrote:
> Hi Chris,
>
> thank you for the tip with geom_line, I only thought about
> stat_function. What is then the difference between both in my
> case? I tried to apply both approaches (geom_line and stat_function)
> but fail somehow with my function... here what I got so far:
>
>
> eq <- function(x,sigma_stat,sigma_mob,p) {
>        (dnorm(x, sd = sigma_stat)*p)+(dnorm(x, sd = sigma_mob)*(1-p))
>        }
>
> sigma_stat <- 10
> sigma_mob <- 100
> p <- 0.3
>
> x <- seq(-1000, 1000, .01)
> tmp <- data.frame(x=x, y=eq(x,sigma_stat,sigma_mob,p))
>
> # First approach (not working)
> plot <- ggplot(tmp, aes(x=x, y=y))
> plot + stat_function(fun=eq(x,sigma_stat,sigma_mob,p))
>
> # Second approach (working)
> plot <- ggplot(tmp, aes(x=x, y=y))
> plot + geom_line()
>
>
> What is the better way to plot the function in general?
>
> best regards,
>
> Johannes
